newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU seeks environmental priorities in East Europe.
newsitem.headline: EU seeks environmental priorities in East Europe.

text.p: The European Union, identifying a series of difficulties facing the former communist bloc, urged membership hopefuls from eastern Europe on Monday to set priorities for their environmental clean up.

At a meeting with the environment ministers of 10 eastern European countries seeking to join the EU, officials from the European Commission said progress was not fast enough in bringing the easterners' policies in line with the EU's.
"A lot has already been achieved, but we have to move forward," EU Environment Commissioner Ritt Bjerregaard told the meeting.

Poland, Hungary, Latvia, Lithuania, Estonia, the Czech republic, Slovakia, Slovenia, Bulgaria and Romania have all been promised eventual EU membership. But they must first bring their laws closer to those of the western bloc.
The Commission, the EU's executive, said a number of "bottlenecks" were slowing things down.
Among them were the size of the task facing the easterners, the limited resources available to them, and the fact that there has not been enough coordination across the region.
"There is an enormous workload for the rather young environmental agencies (of eastern Europe)," one EU official said.
Hans van den Broek, the commissioner responsible for eastern Europe, urged the visiting ministers to make full use of procedures set up by the EU for bringing in the new members.
"In this way we can progressively overcome the ravages caused by decades of damage and neglect under communism and prepare for a future which ensures the well being of our citizens," he said.
